children: Netflix (NFLX) is reportedly cutting 1,000 jobs amid increased streaming competition from Google’s YouTube, Amazon (AMZN), Disney (DIS) and the newly formed Skydance (SKYD), with its co-CEOs telling employees on Wednesday that the company needs to be more “disciplined” in allocating its people and resources.

“Our mission—to entertain the world—is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” co-CEOs Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos wrote in a company email, according to The Wall Street Journal report.

They added that Netflix remains on track to deliver its full-year forecast and “invest aggressively in high-impact areas” to drive growth. “Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors,” the email added.
When Netflix last reported significant layoffs in June 2022, it had recently reported its first quarterly loss of subscribers in more than a decade.
Netflix Job Cuts Come Ahead Of Q3 Earnings

The layoffs come ahead of the company’s third-quarter (Q3) earnings scheduled for next week. Wall Street is expecting Netflix to report earnings per share (EPS) of $0.82 on revenue of $12.88 billion, according to Koyfin.

The cuts also follow comments by Sarandos at the Bloomberg Screen Time conference a few weeks ago. The co-CEO said Netflix was “not growing as fast as I want,” highlighting his ambitions for the streaming business.

Netflix is not the only company looking to cut costs in the media space. Last month, Disney said it would lay off around 300 employees, with the majority of cuts coming from human resources and technology roles. Meanwhile, Amazon cut over 16,000 roles in January, but the cuts were not limited to the Prime Video vertical.
